LHX.sentence: L3Harris jumped this week and is still well below its high from a year ago, so this smallest of the big defense contractors is on a genuine sale — the only soft spot is that their profit margins have thinned a bit lately.

ASML.sentence: ASML barely moved, and while their earnings look expensive on paper, that's just because they're at the bottom of a normal boom-and-bust cycle in chipmaking equipment — they're still the only company making a certain essential machine.

LIN.sentence: Linde had a slightly down week, but nothing's changed — they supply oxygen and other industrial gases on long contracts and nudge prices up steadily, which is the whole story here.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm — the Azure cloud and AI business keeps growing nicely in the background with no real drama this week.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is sitting still while its lab-supplies business grinds along at the bottom of a slow patch, and the hope is that demand picks back up as customers finish working through their stockpiles.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge ticked up and pays a generous dividend from its pipeline toll-road business, though it's priced fairly rather than being a steal right now.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow crashed hard in a single day, which looks alarming, but its automation and AI software sits under long-term corporate and government contracts — so the business is intact even as the stock got slammed.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore barely budged — the miner and commodity trader is priced in the middle of its normal range, neither cheap nor stretched.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta rose this week, and the key thing is that the real price it gets per ton of crushed stone is still creeping upward — each quarry quietly owns its own corner of the map that nobody else can serve cheaply.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA was quiet, but the weakening Mexican peso is the thing to watch since most of its sales are earned in pesos and then converted back to dollars for us.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras slipped a little even though oil prices are high and well above what it costs them to pump — the market keeps applying a discount because the Brazilian government controls the company.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk barely budged and the container-shipping giant is trading well below what its fleet of ships would cost to replace, a sign the market is being cautious about global trade.

MA.sentence: Mastercard rose this week and is actually a touch cheaper than its twin Visa, which is unusual given it usually commands a premium — people keep tapping their cards more than ever.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot company edged up and is now cheaper than it's typically been over the past few years, while hospitals keep doing more operations that each use its supplies.
